title: Turning an active sentence into the passive
intro: Read this before the questions on conversion, negatives, questions and the by-phrase.

blocks.title: four steps
items: 1. Find the **object** of the active sentence.
2. Make it the **subject**. Object pronouns change: me, him, her, us, them become I, he, she, we, they.
3. Write **be in the same tense** as the active verb, then the **past participle**. Be agrees with the new subject.
4. Add the old subject with **by** only if it matters.

blocks.title: one sentence for each tense
items: Present simple: They **make** cars here. → Cars **are made** here.
Past simple: They **built** the house in 1990. → The house **was built** in 1990.
Present continuous: Anna **is painting** the wall. → The wall **is being painted** by Anna.
Present perfect: Someone **has taken** my bag. → My bag **has been taken**.
Future: They **will open** the shop soon. → The shop **will be opened** soon.
Modal: You **must wear** a helmet. → A helmet **must be worn**.

blocks.title: negatives and questions
items: **Negative:** first helper + not: The letter **wasn't sent**. The room **hasn't been cleaned**. The task **won't be done**.
**Question:** first helper in front of the subject: **Was** the letter **sent**? **Has** the room **been cleaned**? **Will** the task **be done**?
**With a question word:** **When was** the window **broken**? **Where were** the photos **taken**?

blocks.title: the by-phrase
items: **Drop the doer** when it is they, someone, people, you or obvious: Someone stole my car → My car **was stolen**.
**Keep by + doer** when it is new or important: *Hamlet* **was written by** Shakespeare.
The by-phrase goes last, and a pronoun there is an object pronoun: **by him**, **by her**, **by them**.

builds: Modal verbs, infinitives and -ing forms in the passive
